memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: That day Joshua took Makkedah. He put the city and its king to the sword and totally destroyed everyone in it. He left no survivors. And he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho. — Josh 10:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter now moves into a rapid summary of city after city falling before Israel, beginning with Makkedah. These are hard verses, and we will not soften the reality of the judgment they describe. We hold them in their redemptive-historical setting: this was God's judgment upon the Canaanite kingdoms, whose wickedness had reached its full measure over centuries of divine patience (Gen 15:16). It is not a template for warfare or for how believers treat others today.

But rather than pass over these summary verses quickly, let us notice one recurring phrase that runs through them: again and again we are told that things happened "as the Lord had commanded" or as had been done before, in obedience to God's word. What stands out in this whole campaign is Joshua's thorough, consistent obedience. He did not conquer some cities carefully and others carelessly. He carried out God's instructions faithfully, city after city, without picking and choosing.

There is a lesson here about consistency in obedience. It is easy to obey God in the areas we find agreeable and to grow slack elsewhere. Joshua's faithfulness was comprehensive; he followed through completely on what God had given him to do. Our obedience, too, is meant to be whole-hearted and consistent, not selective.

This thoroughness ultimately points beyond Joshua to the One who obeyed the Father perfectly and completely. Where every human obedience is partial, Jesus could say, "I have brought you glory on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do" (John 17:4). Joshua's consistent obedience is a faint reflection of Christ's perfect obedience, in which we now stand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your obedience to God consistent, or selective in the areas you find easy?
2. Where might God be calling you to follow through more thoroughly?
3. How does Christ's perfect, finished obedience encourage you when yours falls short?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make my obedience whole-hearted and consistent, not selective. Thank You that Christ obeyed You perfectly on my behalf, and that I stand in His finished work. Amen.
